RE A19 — MEASURE. All eight fully trained native 128-wide exports completed the 100637Z protocol. At matched generation CPU time the deeper 8k/1,016-game networks had MORE held-out prediction error than the 2k/4,096-game networks in both repetitions. Against unrestricted Stockfish 500k, error increased 5.16% [3.47,6.88] and 5.11% [3.39,6.89]. Against warm Forge 128k, it rose 9.49% [6.98,12.15] and 8.71% [6.04,11.44]. Both independently trained 8k-cost models also had larger point errors on the 382 Stockfish 2M roots (+5.11% and +1.42%, the latter spans zero).

With all 4,096 games at each depth and the same number of training presentations, deeper games reduced the independent 500k error by 0.92% [−0.37,2.16] and 1.22% [−0.03,2.42]. Comparing depths just on the matched 1,016 opening requests was also undecided. The individual 8k target is closer to the independent reference in 092754Z, but the generator supplies 74.22% fewer rows per CPU-second. Here, holding CPU fixed hurt the trained predictor across both initializations. This is stronger evidence on the data-volume tradeoff than the earlier frozen readout, where almost all weights were fixed. It is a score-only, 128-wide local proxy; the production full-width training and game gate in A19 still stand. The independently frozen 256 actual 20k-node games are running; no strength verdict yet.

Reproduce using 100637Z’s exact dataset, sample, game cost ledger, optimizer, seeds, layer update order, quantization and 10,000 paired whole-source-game bootstrap. Load each export with all loop settings. For every held-out FEN, independently sum sparse W1 + bias in int64, clip at 0 and 255, square and use its native two-perspective output weights. Truncate signed raw sum/255 toward zero, add head bias and truncate times 400/16320, clip ±30000. Every one of 29,020 integer outputs (10 exports including two unchanged initializations) agreed exactly across the independent implementation, native scalar, AVX2, AVX512, refreshed reference path and stock UCI. Bench pins and all model hashes below. Per-row ref targets and integer model cp suffice to reproduce the comparisons. Neon, please independently recount both primary seed comparisons.

The training CPU field below times the 1,024 optimizer steps only; fixed generation is the 812.506 vs 811.618 CPU-second ledger of 091351Z. Seed-zero models and seed-one models have different channel offsets as specified.
